research.source_name: LADBS Inspections + Certificates of Occupancy (data.lacity.org Socrata)
research.summary: Both target datasets exist on data.lacity.org as live Socrata SODA APIs, refreshed daily (both rowsUpdatedAt 2026-06-08; latest inspection_date 2026-06-06). (1) Building and Safety Inspections (9w5z-rg2h): 11,480,929 rows spanning 2013-01-01 to present, with fields address, permit, permit_status, inspection_date, inspection (type), inspection_result, lat_lon. It has NO native zip or APN column — zip 90272 must be filtered via the computed region column :@computed_region_qz3q_ghft='25066' (verified: 0 post-fire rows missing lat_lon, so the point-in-polygon region is populated). Measured 36,168 inspections in 90272 since 2025-01-07, led by Final (3,882), Footing/Foundation/Slab (2,327), Floor/Roof Diaphragm/Shear Wall (2,289), PLUMBING-Rough (1,720), Excavation/Setback/Form/Re-Bar (1,693). (2) Building and Safety Certificate of Occupancy (3f9m-afei): 38 CofOs issued in 90272 after 2025-06-01 (of which 18 are Bldg-New / 1-or-2 Family Dwelling — the true rebuild-complete signal), 56 since the fire date. Critical join detail verified: inspections.permit uses SPACE separators ('26016 90000 04185') while CofO.pcis_permit and the permits dataset's permit_nbr use DASHES ('26016-90000-04185'); normalizing the separator joins cleanly (tested both directions, including through to APN 4420036007 in permits dataset pi9x-tg5x).

endpoints.name: Building and Safety Inspections (LADBS) — Socrata dataset 9w5z-rg2h

Type breakdown query: ?$select=inspection,count(*) as n&$where=:@computed_region_qz3q_ghft='25066' AND inspection_date>'2025-01-07'&$group=inspection&$order=n DESC. Result domain (90272 post-fire): Approved 8,074; Partial Approval 5,606; Insp Cancelled 3,973; Insp Scheduled 3,805; Corrections Issued 2,923; Not Ready 2,605; Permit Finaled 2,306; Conditional Approval 1,981. headline_numbers: 36,168 LADBS inspections in zip 90272 (computed region 25066) with inspection_date > 2025-01-07 — dataset 9w5z-rg2h, measured 2026-06-09

Top post-fire inspection types in 90272: Final 3,882; Footing/Foundation/Slab 2,327; Floor/Roof Diaphragm/Shear Wall 2,289; PLUMBING-Rough 1,720; Excavation/Setback/Form/Re-Bar 1,693; BUILDING-Rough-Frame 853 — 9w5z-rg2h, 2026-06-09
2,306 inspection rows in 90272 post-fire with inspection_result='Permit Finaled' — 9w5z-rg2h, 2026-06-09
38 Certificates of Occupancy issued in 90272 after 2025-06-01, of which 18 are Bldg-New / 1-or-2 Family Dwelling (rebuilt homes); 56 CofOs since fire date 2025-01-07 — 3f9m-afei, 2026-06-09
Latest 90272 CofO issued 2026-06-03; latest citywide inspection 2026-06-06 — both datasets refresh daily
Inspections dataset is full-history: 11,480,929 rows, 2013-01-01 to present
join_keys: permit number (PCIS): inspections.permit uses SPACES ('26016 90000 04185'); CofO.pcis_permit and permits.permit_nbr use DASHES ('26016-90000-04185') — normalize by replacing separator (verified round-trip: 7 inspection rows matched CofO permit '03010 30000 04720'; permits lookup returned APN 4420036007)

APN: CofO assessor_book(4) + assessor_page(3) + assessor_parcel(3) concatenated = 10-digit APN matching permits.apn format (e.g. 4420+015+001 → '4420015001'); inspections has NO APN — reach it via permit join

address: inspections.address ('1481 N BIENVENEDA AVE') matches permits.primary_address format exactly; CofO address is split into address_start/street_direction/street_name/street_suffix parts and must be assembled
lat/lon: inspections.lat_lon and CofO.latitude_longitude are Socrata location types (point, ~5-decimal precision); permits has separate lat/lon columns
research.recommendation: Use 9w5z-rg2h as the per-parcel construction-progress signal and 3f9m-afei as the completion signal. Pipeline: (1) daily pull of 9w5z-rg2h filtered :@computed_region_qz3q_ghft='25066' AND inspection_date>'2025-01-07' (36k rows, paginate with $limit=50000&$offset or $order=:id); (2) normalize permit spaces→dashes and join to the permits dataset to attach APN, then roll up per APN to a max-stage score: foundation stage = any approved Excavation/Setback/Form/Re-Bar or Footing/Foundation/Slab; framing = BUILDING-Rough-Frame / Floor-Roof Diaphragm-Shear Wall / Wood Frame; MEP = PLUMBING-Rough / ELECTRICAL-Rough / HVAC-Rough; near-complete = Final inspection scheduled/partial; count only inspection_result IN ('Approved','Partial Approval','Conditional Approval','Permit Finaled') as progress evidence. (3) Mark 'complete' from 3f9m-afei where zip_code=90272 AND cofo_issue_date>'2025-01-07' AND permit_type='Bldg-New' AND permit_sub_type='1 or 2 Family Dwelling' (join via pcis_permit or assembled APN), with inspections permit_status/inspection_result='Permit Finaled' as a corroborating signal. Register a free Socrata app token ($$app_token param) for production polling to avoid throttling.
caveats: Inspections dataset (9w5z-rg2h) has no zip_code or APN column. Zip filter relies on Socrata computed region :@computed_region_qz3q_ghft='25066' (note: string value, dataset-specific to data.lacity.org). Verified 0 post-fire rows have null lat_lon, so region coverage is complete, but a handful of boundary parcels geocode into adjacent regions (in the CofO dataset, 11 of ~1,015 zip=90272 rows fell in other region polygons). For parcel-level accuracy, prefer the permit→APN join over the zip-region filter.
Permit-number separator mismatch is the #1 join trap: spaces in inspections, dashes everywhere else. Normalize before joining.
Some inspection rows have NULL inspection_date and sort first under $order=inspection_date DESC — always add 'AND inspection_date IS NOT NULL' when ordering by date.
CofO zip_code is a Socrata number type: query as zip_code=90272 (unquoted); quoting it as a string returns a type error.

Zip 90272 is larger than the burn perimeter, so the 36,168 inspections include normal (non-rebuild) construction; intersect with damage-assessment APNs or post-fire permit numbers (permit prefix 25xxx/26xxx = filed 2025/2026) for true rebuild counts.
Inspection rows include scheduling noise (Insp Scheduled 3,805, Insp Cancelled 3,973, Not Ready 2,605 in the 90272 post-fire slice) — filter on result before treating a row as progress.

CofO dataset's 'CofO Issued' may lag actual occupancy for homes finaled via permit-final without a separate CofO record; cross-check permits.cofo_date (pi9x-tg5x) and inspections permit_status='Permit Finaled'.
No API key required for any endpoint tested, but unauthenticated Socrata requests share a throttling pool — use an app token in production.

research.source_name: Parcel polygons (LA County eGIS / GeoHub) + official Palisades Fire perimeter (CAL FIRE / NIFC WFIGS)
research.summary: LA County's public AGOL org (services.arcgis.com/RmCCgQtiZLDCtblq) hosts a purpose-built 'Palisades Fire Parcels' FeatureServer with 17,471 parcel polygons already clipped to the fire area (APN + situs address), plus a 'Palisades Parcels (with Debris Removal Information)' layer with 12,387 parcels carrying DINS damage class and debris-removal status — 5,877 of which are DAMAGE='Destroyed (>50%)'. This means no fire-perimeter spatial join is needed for the base map; countywide ASSR_PARCELS_25_View (2025 assessor roll, AIN+APN+centroids) is verified as backfill via APN, IN-list, and envelope queries. The official final Palisades perimeter is verified in both CAL FIRE's 2025 California Fire Perimeters View (PALISADES, YEAR_=2025, 23,448.88 GIS acres, alarm 2025-01-07, containment 2025-01-31, INC_NUM 00000738) and NIFC WFIGS (UniqueFireIdentifier 2025-CALFD-000738, IRWIN ID join key); each downloads as a ~386 KB GeoJSON MultiPolygon in ~1s. Full parcel pull is trivially feasible: 2,000 features/page with f=geojson, 1.66 MB and 1.4 s per page, ~9 pages total. APN format is dashed (2177-033-023) everywhere; AIN is undashed (2177033023) on assessor/debris layers. The canonical countywide LACounty_Parcels FeatureServer is token-locked, and LA City GeoHub has no independent city parcel polygon service — the county layers fully cover Pacific Palisades.

All endpoints are anonymous, CORS-served ArcGIS REST — the frontend could even query them directly, but caching is preferred since the parcel geometry and perimeter never change.

research.source_name: LA County Assessor parcel attributes (pre-fire structure characteristics)
research.summary: The historical multi-year "Assessor Parcels Data" no longer lives on Socrata — data.lacounty.gov was migrated off Socrata (Socrata catalog returns "Domain not found") and is now an ArcGIS Hub site. The canonical live source is the LA County ArcGIS FeatureServer table "Assessor Parcel Data (Rolls 2021-2025)" (Parcel_Data_2021_Table/FeatureServer/0), which contains roll years 2021-2025 with AIN, use code/type, year built, SQFTmain, bedrooms, bathrooms, units, full situs address, and parcel centroid lat/lon. The 2024 roll year is a clean pre-fire snapshot: 8,933 records with SitusZIP5=90272 (7,116 of them UseType='SFR'); 2025 roll has 8,937; 2026 roll not yet loaded. The unofficial portal.assessor.lacounty.gov JSON API is fully working: parceldetail?ain= returns live per-parcel detail including current-roll "Misfortune and Calamity" reason codes, and a separate MncStatus endpoint returns per-parcel M&C claim status (e.g. claimStatus "Approved") — a direct fire-damage/reassessment flag. No property-photo API exists; only a pictometry-signed-url endpoint for EagleView aerial imagery.

research.source_name: CAL FIRE DINS structure damage assessments — 2025 Palisades Fire
research.summary: The authoritative per-structure damage data lives in CAL FIRE's ArcGIS Online org (services1.arcgis.com/jUJYIo9tSA7EHvfZ). The best endpoint is the statewide POSTFIRE_MASTER_DATA_SHARE FeatureServer (the official dataset behind data.ca.gov's "CAL FIRE Damage Inspection (DINS) Data"), filtered to INCIDENTNAME='Palisades' / INCIDENTNUM='CALFD 000738': 12,137 records with full schema including DAMAGE, STRUCTURETYPE, STRUCTURECATEGORY, APN, SITEADDRESS, LATITUDE/LONGITUDE, and NUMBEROFUNITPERSTRUCTURE. Damage breakdown: 6,845 Destroyed (>50%), 732 Affected, 171 Minor, 72 Major, 56 Inaccessible, 4,261 No Damage. Destroyed single-family-residence structures: 5,066 (STRUCTURETYPE LIKE 'Single Family Residence%'); 5,428 if using STRUCTURECATEGORY='Single Residence' (which also sweeps in mobile/motor homes). Coverage spans the entire fire footprint — LA City Pacific Palisades plus Malibu, Topanga, and unincorporated areas — but the CITY field is the postal community, not legal jurisdiction; jurisdiction must come from a parcel join (LA County's 2025_Parcels_with_DINS_data layer 5 has LCITY: 9,269 Los Angeles / 1,704 unincorporated 'UA PALISADES' / 1,412 Malibu parcels). The widely-cited incident-specific DINS_2025_Palisades_Public_View exposes only DAMAGE + STRUCTURETYPE (no APN/address), so use the master share for joins.

Destroyed by structure type (top): SFR Multi Story 2,741; SFR Single Story 2,325; Utility/Misc 1,120; Mobile Home Double Wide 236; Multi-Family Multi Story 121; Commercial Single Story 85; School 51
Destroyed by postal city (DTSC March-2025 snapshot): Pacific Palisades 5,484 / Malibu 1,282 / Topanga 70 / Santa Monica 6
All-records by postal city: Pacific Palisades 9,030 / Malibu 2,220 / Topanga 400 / Los Angeles 228 / Santa Monica 82 / blank 118
Palisades parcels by legal jurisdiction (LA County parcel layer, updated 2026-05-19): City of LA 9,269 / unincorporated 'UA PALISADES' 1,704 / City of Malibu 1,412
join_keys: APN — string, 10 digits, no dashes (e.g. '4412018007') in master field APN / DTSC field APN; matches LA County assessor AIN (parcel layer fields AIN_1/APN_1, where APN_1 is dashed format) — only ~3 Palisades records have blank APN

SITEADDRESS — full one-line address 'NUMBER STREET, CITY, CA ZIP' (e.g. '556 VIA DE LA PAZ, PACIFIC PALISADES, CA 90272'); components also available (STREETNUMBER, STREETNAME, STREETTYPE, CITY, ZIPCODE)
LATITUDE / LONGITUDE — WGS84 doubles on every record (also point geometry, f=geojson supported)
GLOBALID — UUID stable across the CAL FIRE master share and the DINS_2025_Palisades_Public_View (verified same id space); use to join the two CAL FIRE products
No permit number in DINS — join to permits via APN or normalized address
research.recommendation: Use POSTFIRE_MASTER_DATA_SHARE/FeatureServer/0 with where=INCIDENTNAME='Palisades' AND INCIDENTSTARTDATE>DATE '2025-01-01' (equivalently INCIDENTNUM='CALFD 000738') as the tracker's baseline layer: it defines the universe of damaged/destroyed structures and supplies DAMAGE, STRUCTURETYPE/STRUCTURECATEGORY, APN, SITEADDRESS, and lat/lon for joining to permits and debris-removal data. Ingest once (data is final; page 2000 records at a time with resultOffset, or grab the CNRA hub GeoJSON export) and re-check the layer's editingInfo.dataLastEditDate occasionally. Key the tracker's lots on APN (string, no dashes), fall back to normalized SITEADDRESS, then nearest-point lat/lon. For the map's 'destroyed lots' universe use DAMAGE='Destroyed (>50%)' (6,845 structures; note multiple DINS points can share one APN — outbuildings etc. — so dedupe to parcel level, preferring the primary STRUCTURECATEGORY in ('Single Residence','Multiple Residence','Mixed Commercial/Residential','Nonresidential Commercial')). For jurisdiction (LA City vs Malibu vs unincorporated), do NOT rely on the DINS CITY field (it is the postal community); join APN to LA County's 2025_Parcels_with_DINS_data layer 5 LCITY field or spatially join city boundaries.
caveats: The famous incident URL (DINS_2025_Palisades_Public_View) now exposes only 4 fields (OBJECTID, GLOBALID, DAMAGE, STRUCTURETYPE) — no APN/address/units. Use the statewide master share for full attributes.

Master share is statewide and multi-incident: always filter on INCIDENTNAME + INCIDENTSTARTDATE (there are other fires named 'Palisades' historically) — verified that the 2025 filter resolves to a single INCIDENTNUM 'CALFD 000738'.

Record-count discrepancy is explained: master 12,137 vs public view 12,081 = 56 'Inaccessible' records excluded by the public view's definition query (EDITSTATUS='Approved' AND SHARED='Yes' AND REPORTED='Yes').

Damage-level label text differs between products: master uses 'Affected (>0-10%)' / 'Major (25-50%)'; the public view domain uses 'Affected (1-9%)' / 'Major (26-50%)'. 'Destroyed (>50%)' is identical in both. Match on prefix (Destroyed/Major/Minor/Affected) when normalizing.

DINS is structure-level, not parcel-level: one APN can have multiple points (house + outbuildings); 1,120 of the 6,845 destroyed records are 'Utility Misc Structure'. Dedupe by APN for a lot-level map.
NUMBEROFUNITPERSTRUCTURE is unreliable — 0 even on destroyed single-family homes in sampled records. Get unit counts from assessor data instead.
CITY field is postal community (Pacific Palisades, Malibu, Topanga...), not legal jurisdiction; COMMUNITY field is ~94% blank and contains free-text junk. No jurisdiction field exists in DINS.

DINS data is effectively frozen (assessment complete); the public Palisades view last changed 2025-06-23 and the DTSC full-attribute mirror is a 2025-03-21 snapshot. Treat damage data as static input, not a live feed.

maxRecordCount is 2000 on the master layer (16,000 on the public view layer) — paginate with resultOffset/resultRecordCount or use the CNRA hub bulk download (that download URL itself was not curl-verified).
ASSESSEDIMPROVEDVALUE and YEARBUILT come from assessor roll at inspection time; fine for display, but prefer live assessor data for valuation.

research.source_name: LA City (LADBS) building permits — Socrata + GeoHub fire-rebuild feeds
research.summary: Found and curl-verified four machine-readable feeds. The standout is a purpose-built ArcGIS FeatureServer on LA City GeoHub, LADBS_WF_Fire_Data_Palisades_Recovery_Area (4,857 point records, last edited 2026-06-10, i.e. refreshed daily), which contains exactly the tracker's data model: per-permit milestone dates (SUBMIT/PC_APPROVED/CORRECTIONS/ISSUE/COFO), PERMIT_STATUS, a PALISADES_WF_REBUILD flag (1,302 rebuild permits issued + 494 rebuild plan-check applications), ELIGIBILITY (2,097 Eligible / 523 Ineligible / 2,237 Pending), APN, lat/lon, and days-to-milestone metrics. Socrata datasets pi9x-tg5x (issued) and gwh9-jnip (submitted), both 2020-to-present, provide full citywide permit detail: 3,825 permits issued and 4,796 submitted in zip 90272 since 2025-01-07, of which 1,168 issued are Bldg-New; work_desc contains explicit '**2025 WILDFIRE**' / 'WILDFIRE REBUILD' markers (2,861 issued permits match FIRE/REBUILD). Socrata 3f9m-afei (Certificates of Occupancy) gives the completion signal with contractor detail: 56 CofOs in 90272 since the fire, 24 for new buildings. LADBS's own ePlanLA dashboard is Angeleno-Account login-gated (no public API); the public 'Pacific Palisades Recovery by the Numbers' dashboard is driven by the GeoHub FeatureServer above, which we hit directly.

join_keys: PCIS permit number (5-5-5 format, e.g. 25010-10000-05963): GeoHub PERMIT = Socrata permit_nbr = CofO pcis_permit. Primary join key. Note GeoHub plan-check rows and permit rows share a stem; supplementals increment the middle segment.

APN: GeoHub layer is hyphenated county format (4423-012-006); Socrata permit datasets are 10-digit unhyphenated (4423012006); CofO dataset splits it as assessor_book(4)+assessor_page(3)+assessor_parcel(3); parcels layer has both AIN and APN. Normalize by stripping hyphens / concatenating to 10 digits.
Address: GeoHub ADDRESS vs Socrata primary_address (both uppercase house-number + dir + street); needs light normalization (suffix, unit ranges like '3500 W 63RD ST 1-15').
Lat/lon: GeoHub LAT/LON (WGS84 attributes) and Socrata lat/lon + geolocation Point; Socrata type_lat_lon indicates geocode basis (ADDRESS).

research.recommendation: Use the GeoHub FeatureServer LADBS_WF_Fire_Data_Palisades_Recovery_Area/0 as the tracker's primary per-lot status source — it is refreshed daily, already filtered to the Palisades recovery area, and natively encodes the tracker's color-coding stages: Plans Submitted -> Plan Check in Progress / Corrections Issued -> Plans Approved & Permit Not Issued -> Plans Approved & Permit Issued -> COFO_DATE set (complete), plus PALISADES_WF_REBUILD and ELIGIBILITY flags. Pull it nightly with f=geojson&outSR=4326, paginating with resultOffset (page size 1000). Enrich each record via permit-number join to Socrata pi9x-tg5x / gwh9-jnip (valuation, square_footage, du_changed, council district, official status_desc) and 3f9m-afei (CofO number/date, contractor) — but treat the Socrata trio as ~2 weeks lagged relative to the GeoHub layer. Paint destroyed lots using LA_Parcels_in_Palisades_Fire_Perimeter polygons (DINS DAMAGE field) joined on normalized APN/AIN, treating that layer as a static base snapshot. Validate the pipeline against the public 'Pacific Palisades Recovery by the Numbers' dashboard since it reads the same FeatureServer.
caveats: Socrata datasets (pi9x-tg5x, gwh9-jnip, 3f9m-afei) lag real time by ~2 weeks (max refresh_time 2026-05-25 vs GeoHub layer edited 2026-06-10). Use GeoHub for current status, Socrata for enrichment.
GeoHub layer mixes TYPE='Plan Check Application' and TYPE='Permit' rows for the same project — dedupe/roll up by permit-number stem or PROJECT before counting lots.
GeoHub layer covers the 'Palisades Recovery Area', which includes non-rebuild activity (PALISADES_WF_REBUILD='No' = 3,061 rows, e.g. repairs/pools in standing homes) — filter or weight accordingly.
Zip 90272 is a proxy, not the fire footprint: it includes undamaged Palisades blocks and excludes Malibu/unincorporated parcels burned in the same fire (those are LA County EPIC-LA jurisdiction).
APN formats differ across feeds (hyphenated vs 10-digit vs book/page/parcel) — normalization required before joining.
GeoHub native spatial reference is EPSG 2229 (ft) — always request outSR=4326 or use the LAT/LON attribute fields.
ArcGIS date fields are epoch milliseconds; Socrata dates are ISO floating timestamps.
LA_Parcels_in_Palisades_Fire_Perimeter last edited 2025-10-08; its Has_Permit/Permit_Status fields are stale — do not use them for live status.
ePlanLA (official LADBS portal) is login-gated; no public LADBS API beyond the GeoHub layer and Socrata exports was found.
Unauthenticated Socrata works but is throttled; register an app token for the nightly pipeline.

research.source_name: LA County permits (EPIC-LA, unincorporated) + City of Malibu rebuild permits
research.summary: Both non-LA-City jurisdictions in the Palisades Fire footprint have live, machine-readable permit data, so v1 of the tracker CAN cover the full footprint. (1) LA County unincorporated (Sunset Mesa/Topanga): EPIC-LA is Tyler EnerGov (not Accela), and LA County DPW publishes a nightly-refreshed hosted FeatureServer "EPIC-LA Case History" (895,171 cases total) with dedicated disaster-rebuild fields — DISASTER_TYPE, REBUILD_PROGRESS, milestone columns, MAIN_AIN (APN) and point geometry. Filtering DISASTER_TYPE='Palisades Fire (01-2025)' returns 398 cases with a full stage breakdown (131 zoning cleared, 103 plans received, 63 in construction, 25 permits issued, 11 completed, etc.); data last edited 2026-06-09 (today). (2) City of Malibu: maliburebuilds.org embeds a city-hosted ASP.NET/Kendo app (mlb-pptsrv.ci.malibu.ca.us) whose backing JSON endpoints are publicly curl-able with no auth: a per-parcel marker feed (264 rebuild cases with lat/lon, APN, case number, status), an aggregate pie (219 projects), and permits-issued-by-type (Building 230, Debris Removal 214, etc.). The county's official "Permitting Progress Dashboard" is a Power BI Gov embed (no API) but is redundant given the FeatureServer. LA County's open-data portal is now ArcGIS Hub, not Socrata — no Socrata permit dataset exists.

research.summary: The City of LA's official "LA Strong" Palisades Recovery Dashboard (recovery.lacity.gov) is backed by a public ArcGIS FeatureServer (LADBS_WF_Fire_Data_Palisades_Recovery_Area) that I curl-verified live with data last edited 2026-06-10 — it is THE validation baseline and also a primary per-permit data source (APN, address, lat/lon, submit/plan-check/issue/CofO dates, status). research.recommendation: Use the LADBS_WF_Fire_Data_Palisades_Recovery_Area FeatureServer/0 as both a primary ingestion source and the validation oracle: after each pipeline run, re-run the server-side group-by queries (PERMIT_STATUS, PERMIT_TYPE, COFO_DATE/ISSUE_DATE not-null, distinct-APN counts) and require exact reconciliation with the pipeline's computed aggregates under identical filters. Display headline cards that match the official dashboard's framing (applications, permits issued, under construction, CofOs) but compute 'homes' figures from Bldg-New + distinct APN to avoid the all-permit-types inflation that confuses news comparisons. Use the 2025_Parcels_with_DINS_data polygons as the lot base layer (DAMAGE_1 for destroyed status, TaxRateCity for jurisdiction). Cross-check monthly against the Palisadian-Post/Pali Builds table (expect our CofO count >= their last monthly figure) and Crosstown's monthly time series. Product gaps to exploit vs all prior art: (1) nobody shows a per-lot color-coded map of rebuild stage — official dashboards are aggregate charts, community trackers are tables; (2) adopt Palisadian-Post's velocity medians (submit-to-permit, permit-to-CofO days — already computable from DAYS_TO_* and date fields); (3) cover the whole fire perimeter (city + Malibu + unincorporated) with explicit 'no live data' styling for non-city jurisdictions; (4) update at least daily — the official feed supports it.

research.source_name: Imagery: Esri Wayback pre-fire thumbnails, NOAA/Maxar post-fire aerials, MapLibre basemaps
research.summary: All three imagery tiers are live and curl-verified. (1) Pre-fire: Esri Wayback serves keyless JPEG XYZ tiles; the release labeled 2024-12-12 (#16453) is the last pre-fire release, and over Pacific Palisades it 301-redirects to release #32553 (2024-08-15), the actual last pre-fire capture — z18 and z19 tiles both return 200 image/jpeg with CORS *. The latest release #10842 (2026-05-28) resolves to #49059 (2026-04-30) and shows current post-fire conditions, so Wayback alone gives both before and now states. (2) Post-fire: NOAA Emergency Response Imagery for the '2025_eri' event exposes 30 XYZ tile services on stormscdn.ngs.noaa.gov; 7 cover the Palisades test point, including six Maxar layers (Jan 9-20, 2025, maxzoom 19) and NOAA's own 20250128a-rgb flight (maxzoom 21) — tiles verified at z18/z19 with CORS *. Source GeoTIFFs are in the public noaa-eri-pds S3 bucket. Maxar Open Data has a full STAC catalog for event WildFires-LosAngeles-Jan-2025 (license CC-BY-NC-4.0) with range-readable visual COGs (0.6 m GSD) verified over Palisades. NAIP is pre-fire-only: latest published quad at the point is 2022-05-11 (USGS ImageServer and Planetary Computer both confirm; no 2025/2026 NAIP exists yet). (3) Basemap: OpenFreeMap is the clear winner — keyless, no rate limits, free including commercial use, style JSON + TileJSON + z14 vector tile all verified with CORS *; Carto GL styles also work keyless as fallback; Protomaps hosted API requires a key (403 without) but daily 136 GB planet PMTiles builds are openly downloadable for self-hosting; Esri vector basemaps require a token (499).
